body: SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations 2015. UPSI (Reg 2(1)(n)) is non-public information about a company or its securities likely to materially affect the price, ordinarily including financial results, dividends, capital-structure changes, M&A, delisting, disposals and KMP changes. 'Generally available information' (Reg 2(1)(e)) is information accessible to the public on a non-discriminatory basis; the May-2024 amendment excludes unverified media reports. An insider is anyone in possession of or with access to UPSI, however obtained, so an outsider who extracts unreleased sales or order numbers from an employee becomes an insider. Trading while in possession (Reg 4) and procuring or communicating UPSI (Reg 3) are prohibited. Safe practice: ask about your own observations and the counter-party's own business (a dealer's own sales and stock), never an employee's knowledge of unreleased company numbers or deals. If UPSI is volunteered, stop, note it, and do not trade until it is public. Never pay insiders. Treat expert-network calls with current employees as high risk. Keep a dated mosaic log. India has no explicit mosaic-theory safe harbour, so be conservative. Not legal advice.
title: SEBI PIT rules: where scuttlebutt becomes insider trading

body: RULE: a high ROE is a result to be explained, not a quality. Decompose it (DuPont: margin x asset turn x leverage) and ask which leg carries it. SUSPECT WHEN: (1) CFO is far below PAT for several years in a non-lender (profits not becoming cash); (2) ROE comes from leverage (equity a thin slice; NBFC leverage >7-8x; DHFL ~10x); (3) in a lender, ROE is lifted by low provisions on a fast-growing book: new loans have not had time to default (Yes Bank FY18: ROE 17.7%, GNPA 1.28%, loans +54%, while RBI's divergence reports showed NPAs under-recognised by Rs 4,177 cr in FY16 and Rs 6,355 cr in FY17); (4) margins/ROCE far above peers in a commodity-like business with no visible mechanism (Vakrangee ROCE ~40% in rural kiosks); (5) ROE flattered by buybacks or a shrinking equity base from write-offs. BENIGN WHEN: ROE comes from high margins or asset turns with low debt and is matched by CFO (Page 45-69% ROCE, Pidilite, APL Apollo at 5-8% margins but ~0 WC days), or in a bank from low-cost deposits, granular seasoned retail loans and stable credit costs (HDFC Bank 16-20% for a decade). TEST: 5-year CFO/PAT; leverage; for lenders: loan growth vs system (>2-3x system = red), lagged NPA (NPA / loans of 2-3 years ago), divergence notes, CASA, top-20 exposures; compare ROE with the best peer and ask why it is higher.

data.benign_if: margin/turn-driven with CFO; bank with CASA + seasoned retail
suspect_if: lender growth >2-3x system with low NPA
ROCE far above peers without mechanism

title: When a high ROE is suspect: CFO << PAT, leverage, under-provisioning, fast lender growth
